title: Adaptive Cost Gatekeeper - launch kit and PRD
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Summary: The Adaptive Cost Gatekeeper (ACG) is a product initiative to provide per-request, policy-driven gating of model variant choice and runtime fidelity to meet customer SLOs while minimizing unit cost. This doc bundles the product overview, PRD, high-level design, rollout roadmap, pricing/packaging guidance, and v1.0 release notes into a single launch kit for cross-functional teams.

Problem statement

Teams building LLM features often trade latency and quality for cost manually: maintaining multiple model variants and bespoke routing logic. Customers need a thin, centrally managed service that automatically chooses an acceptable model/fidelity per request based on explicit policies (latency, cost budget, regulatory guardrails). Without this capability customers either overprovision (pay too much) or under-deliver (miss SLOs).

Goals and success metrics (product-level)

- Primary goal: Reduce billed per-token cost for typical conversational workloads by 15–30% for customers that opt in to ACG within 90 days of GA.
- Shield customer application-level SLOs: 99.95% availability, p99 latency degradation of route <= +50ms relative to pinned baseline for small (<= 128 tokens) responses.
- Fallback correctness: fallback-to-safe-variant rate <= 0.5% under normal operation.
- Cost regressions: detect and alert if per-tenant cost delta > 20% vs baseline within 24 hours.

User personas

- ML/Platform engineer (primary): integrates Gatekeeper into routing, configures policies, reviews telemetry.
- Product engineer: sets per-route cost budgets and fidelity constraints.
- Customer success / Solutions (CS/SE): uses playbooks to advise customers on policy selection and commercial options.

Must-have requirements (MUST)

1) Runtime decisioning: ACG must accept an HTTP/GRPC evaluation API that returns a routing decision (variant id, fidelity profile, estimated cost delta) in <= 10ms median.
2) Policy engine: support declarative policies: latency_budget_ms, cost_budget_usd_per_1000_tokens, safety_labels (e.g. pii_prohibited), regional_affinity.
3) Observability: emit per-decision telemetry with labels: tenant_id, route, decision_reason, estimated_cost, chosen_variant, p99_est_latency. Must integrate into Console dashboards and billing reconciliation.
4) Fallbacks: automatic safe fallback policies that prefer compatibility (API contract) and safety over cost savings.
5) Auditing & SSO: decisions must be auditable for 90 days and visible in tenant audit logs.

Should-have (SHOULD)

- Local simulator: customer-facing simulation CLI to run synthetic traffic through policies and produce cost/latency impact projections.
- Canary rollout hooks and feature flags per-tenant.
- Suggestion engine: using Optimize signals to recommend policies based on historic traffic.

Design overview (high level)

Components (service names):
- cost-gatekeeper-api: evaluation endpoint (HTTP/gRPC).
- policy-store: durable rules DB with versioning and rollouts.
- cost-sim: simulation engine (offline and CLI).
- variant-selector: real-time selector that queries pricing and runtime profiles.
- routing-orchestrator: issues actual routing decisions to serving runtime via routing policy service.
- telemetry-ingest: structured decision telemetry; feeds Console and billing pipelines.

Data flow (summary):
1) Request arrives at routing tier.
2) routing-tier calls cost-gatekeeper-api with attributes: route, tenant, input_size, user_fidelity_hint, session_state.
3) cost-gatekeeper evaluates policies (policy-store) and runtime profiles (variant-selector) and returns decision object.
4) routing-tier implements decision (route to model variant / apply fidelity knobs) and records telemetry.

Decision latency SLAs and thresholds (configurable):
- Decision median <= 10ms; p95 <= 40ms.
- For session-affine fast paths (session pinned) decision median <= 4ms.

Policy examples (text table):
- Row format (policy_name | constraints):
  - default-cost-guard | latency_budget_ms:200, cost_budget_usd_per_1000_tokens:0.30, safety: allow_all
  - regulatory-eu-strict | latency_budget_ms:250, cost_budget:0.45, region_affinity: eu-west-1, safety: pii_prohibited

API surface (example)

Request (pseudo-JSON in one line):
{ "tenant_id": "acme-inc", "route": "/chat/gen", "input_tokens": 42, "session_id": "s-1234", "hints": {"max_accept_delay_ms":150} }

Response (pseudo-JSON):
{ "decision": "use_variant:v3-q4", "fidelity_profile": "pruned-encoder:low-attn", "estimated_cost_usd": "0.00027", "decision_reason": "meets_latency_and_cost" }

Billing and telemetry hooks

- Every decision emits telemetry keys: tenant_id, route, decision_id (uuid), estimated_cost_usd, chosen_variant, policy_applied, timestamp.
- Billing pipeline must consume estimated_cost_usd tags to attribute pre-billing estimates for feature-level cost visibility. Final billing still reconciled from token meters.

Operational controls and safety

- Emergency kill-switch per-tenant: immediate bypass to pinned variant (owner: eng-sre).
- Safety precedence: policies marked safety:strict override cost budgets.
- Quota enforcement: ACG integrates with rate-limiter to ensure cost policies do not cause quota escalation.

Roadmap and rollout plan (Q4 2026 -> Q2 2027)

Phase 0 (spec & prototypes) Q4 2026 (owner: product + eng-platform)
1) Finalize policy language and config schema.
2) Build minimal cost-sim prototype and CLI.
3) Integrate prototype into internal developer sandbox for experiments.

Phase 1 (experimental alpha) Q1 2027 (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
1) Implement cost-gatekeeper-api with in-memory policy-store.
2) Expose CLI simulator to 10 internal teams.
3) First telemetry dashboard iteration in Console.

Phase 2 (private beta) Q2 2027 (owner: product + eng-sre)
1) Persistent policy-store, versioned rollouts, canary scheduler.
2) Billing integration for estimated_cost signals.
3) Beta customers (3 tenants) with SLA experiments.

Phase 3 (GA) Q3 2027 (owner: go-to-market)
1) GA SDKs and docs, SLA contract addendum, pricing bundles.
2) Expand CS playbook and migration assistance.

Pricing and packaging notes (initial guidance)

Pricing objectives: make ACG accessible to developers while capturing commercial value for enterprise tenants needing SLA-backed guarantees.

Suggested packaging: 
- Developer tier (free/low-cost): access to cost-sim and soft decisions (no SLA).
- Team tier (metered): metered per-decision charge + small percentage of cost-savings captured as "optimization fee" (e.g. 5% of measured monthly savings compared to baseline).
- Enterprise tier (reserved + SLA): monthly seat + guaranteed decision latency SLOs + optional revenue-share escalation for delivered savings exceeding threshold. Includes audit log retention and prioritized support.

Billing model notes: estimated_cost_usd is used for visibility only; final billed tokens still come from token meters. For Team/Enterprise tiers we instrument a reconciliation window (7 days) to account for differences between estimated and actual.

Commercial guardrails and discounts:
- Beta program: waive metered fees for first 3 months; apply professional services credits for migration.
- Enterprise discounts for multi-tenant reserved capacity commitments.

Release notes - v0.1 (alpha)

Released components:
- cost-gatekeeper-api (alpha): in-memory policies, basic decisioning.
- cost-sim CLI: run simulated traffic profiles; outputs estimated cost delta and latency histogram.
- Console dashboard (alpha): per-decision telemetry feed and heatmaps for policy hot spots.

Known limitations:
- No persistent policy-store in alpha; policies are ephemeral.
- Estimated cost uses static runtime profiles — accuracy expected +/- 15% in alpha.
- No automated billing reconciliation; manual reports required for early adopters.

Migration & integration playbook (high level)

1) Audit current routing: identify routes that have median response length <= 512 tokens and that would benefit from variant selection. (owner: customer/CS)
2) Run cost-sim with 2 weeks of synthetic traffic to estimate savings. (owner: customer/SE with support)
3) Apply conservative policy: start with cost_budget that yields <= 5% predicted quality delta. Use canary on 1% traffic. (owner: eng/SE)
4) Monitor telemetry for 72 hours. If errors/fallbacks exceed thresholds, revert to pinned variant. (owner: eng-sre)

Open questions and risks

- Accuracy of cost estimates vs actual billing (risk: customer distrust). Mitigation: short reconciliation windows and transparent estimation error bands.
- Policy complexity vs usability: if the policy language is too expressive, customers will misconfigure. Mitigation: create safe presets and guided policy templates.
- Performance overhead: added decisioning latency could compound p99s. Mitigation: inline fast paths and session caching.

Next steps (next 30 days)

- Approve policy schema and commit to implementation plan (product + eng-platform).
- Build alpha cost-sim and surface it to internal developer sandbox.
- Prepare initial pricing brief for finance and go-to-market.

Attachments and references

- Prototype API spec (inline above) and simulated cost CSV example.
- Related internal design docs: see related_pages field.

Appendix: sample policy YAML (example)

policy_id: default-cost-guard
priority: 10
constraints:
  latency_budget_ms: 200
  cost_budget_usd_per_1000_tokens: 0.30
  safety: allow_all
fallback: "pinned-variant"
rollout: 
  default: 0.0
  canary: 0.01
